sentences.text: Mihir Das vs Unknown on 7 October, 2024

Author: Tirthankar Ghosh
Bench: Tirthankar Ghosh
07.10.2024 Serial no. 7 Ct.-35 [G.S.D] Cra (Sb) 159 of 2024 With Cran 1 of 2024 In Re: An
application under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973/Section 430 of the Bharatiya
Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
And

In the matter of : Mihir Das ... ... appellant Mr. Navanil De Mr. Rajeshar Chakraborty ... for the
appellant Mr. Rudradipta Nandy, ld. App Ms. Manisha Sharma ... for the State Mr. De, learned
advocate, appearing for the appellant, submits that the present case was initiated in the year
October, 2006 and charge-sheet was submitted on or before December, 2006 under Sections
498A/304B/302 of the Ipc.

The appellant has been convicted and sentenced to suffer for a period of 7 years in respect of the offence under Section 304B of the IPC and for a period of three years in respect of the offence under Section 498A of the IPC.
The records reflect that the appellant was throughout on bail during the trial and, as such, the learned advocate prays for releasing the appellant/petitioner on any condition.

Mr. Nandy, learned advocate, appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the contentions so advanced on behalf of the appellant and submits that within four years of marriage, the unfortunate incident took place and there were demand of dowry as is reflected from the evidence of the case.
I find that the sentence so imposed by the learned trial court is for a fixed period of term and the appellant has been before the court for more than 17 years.

Having considered the period for which the trial has been continuing for 17 years and the sentence so imposed is for a fixed period of time, I am of the view that the appeal cannot be disposed of within this year, so it would be fit and proper, in the interest of justice, that the appellant be released on bail.
Accordingly, the prayer for bail in connection with appeal of the petitioner/appellant is
Allowed.

Accordingly, the appellant/petitioner (Mihir Das) is directed to furnish bond of Rs.10,000/- with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned CJM,
Alipore.

If, on bail, the appellant/petitioner shall appear before the learned trial court being the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, 7th Fast Track Court, Alipore, South 24 Parganas once in a month till further orders of this court.
